basis.governing_question: How can Grupo Vale integrate sales, purchasing and finance of its three acquired regional food distributors into its own, starting with the first company?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Assess how sales, purchasing and finance run at each acquired company and where they differ from Grupo Vale.

gate.label: Go/no-go on design
gate.decision: Go ahead with design on the priority gaps in sales, purchasing and finance?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define how each acquired company moves onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems, and the integration plan for all three.

gate.label: Go/no-go on cutover
gate.decision: Go or no-go on moving the first company onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Move the first company's sales, purchasing and finance onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems and confirm they run.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the first-company result and the integration plan to take to the board?

workstreams.name: Current state, two companies
workstreams.answers: How do sales, purchasing and finance run today at the first company and one other acquired company?
activities: Interview the people who do the work in each company
Walk through sales, purchasing and finance processes
Collect operational and cost data for each company

workstreams.name: Third company, gap ranking
workstreams.answers: How do sales, purchasing and finance run at the third company, and which gaps to Grupo Vale matter most?
activities: Interview staff and collect data at the third company
Compare all three companies with Grupo Vale's processes
Rank the gaps for the go/no-go on design

workstreams.name: Design, first two companies
workstreams.answers: How should the first company and one other move sales, purchasing and finance onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems?
activities: Detail target processes with each company's leaders
Map each company's processes onto Grupo Vale's systems
List the data and system changes each move needs

workstreams.name: Design, third company
workstreams.answers: How should the third company's sales, purchasing and finance move onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems?
activities: Apply design choices from the first two companies
Detail target processes with the company's leaders
Map the company's processes onto Grupo Vale's systems

workstreams.name: Integration plan and review
workstreams.answers: What integration plan for the three companies, with sequence and risks, can the board approve?
activities: Sequence the moves of the three companies and list risks
Set the readiness checks for the first company's cutover
Review designs and plan with the CEO, CFO and company heads

workstreams.name: Cutover, first two areas
workstreams.answers: Do two of the first company's sales, purchasing and finance areas run on Grupo Vale's processes and systems after cutover?
activities: Prepare the two areas for cutover with the process owners
Move the two areas onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems
Track live operating data against the cutover checks

workstreams.name: Cutover, third area
workstreams.answers: Does the last of the first company's sales, purchasing and finance areas run on Grupo Vale's processes and systems?
activities: Apply what the first two areas showed to the third area
Move the third area onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems
Track live results against the readiness checks

workstreams.name: Stabilization, plan update
workstreams.answers: Which open issues remain after cutover, and does the integration plan hold up against the first company's results?
activities: Close open issues with the people using the new processes
Test first-company results against the success criteria
Update the integration plan with what the cutover showed

deliverables.name: Priority gaps to Grupo Vale across three companies
Target processes and system mapping, first two companies
Target processes and system mapping, third company
Cutover readiness checks for the first company
Integration plan and cutover decision pack
Cutover readiness and progress report, first two areas
Go-live record for two areas of the first company
Go-live record for the third area
First-company results and updated integration plan

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start the diagnostic and agree access
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Will each company open its sales, purchasing and finance data and staff to the team?
agenda: Present the three phases and the diagnostic in weeks 1-3
Align on the data and people needed at each company
Decide on access to sales, purchasing and finance data and staff

events.label: Go/no-go on design
events.purpose: Decide whether to go ahead with design
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Go ahead with design on the priority gaps in sales, purchasing and finance?
agenda: Present the current-state baseline for the first two companies
Review the priority gaps to Grupo Vale across three companies
Decide on going ahead with design on the priority gaps

events.label: Go/no-go on cutover
events.purpose: Decide whether to start the first cutover
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Go or no-go on moving the first company onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems?
agenda: Present target processes and system mapping, all three companies
Review the readiness checks and the integration plan decision pack
Decide on the cutover of the first company

events.label: Check-in: cutover progress
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Is cutover progress on track to start stabilization and the plan update in week 11?
agenda: Present the cutover readiness and progress report, first two areas
Discuss open issues and early results that feed the plan update
Confirm progress before stabilization and the plan update begin

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Approve the result and plan for the board
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Approve the first-company result and the integration plan to take to the board?
agenda: Present first-company results, go-live records and the updated plan
Review the open-issues log and closure record
Decide on the plan to take to the board on 29 January 2027

deadline.text: Before the board meeting on 29 January 2027

architect_notes: The work counted needs 19-28 weeks, more than the 12 planned: cut scope, run more at once, or extend.
Engagement length is assumed: phases are cut to the 12 weeks before the 29 January 2027 board meeting, but the work sizes at 19-28 weeks.
Conflict: the board approves the plan after these phases, yet Implementation moves the first company onto Grupo Vale's systems before it; confirm that order.
Departure from operating_model_redesign: Implementation added, and no whole-organization target model in Design, because Grupo Vale's own processes and systems are the target.
Implementation is sized for the first company only, as the brief states; which company goes first is not named and must be confirmed.
Implementation work units are the architect's estimates, not library units; confirm 3-4 weeks per process area with the partner.

sub_questions.question: How do sales, purchasing and finance work today at each acquired company, compared with Grupo Vale?
How should each acquired company's sales, purchasing and finance move onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems?
What integration plan for the three companies, with sequence and risks, can the board approve?
Do the first company's sales, purchasing and finance run on Grupo Vale's processes and systems after cutover?

drivers.evidence: Grupo Vale has bought three regional food distributors

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Unit diagnosed (interviews, process walk-throughs, workload and cost baseline)

phases.why: Two companies are diagnosed side by side, then the third; sales, purchasing and finance are covered in each walk-through.

phases.name: Design

work.unit: Unit-level design detailed with the unit's leaders

phases.why: Units designed two at a time, then plan and review. Minimum is below typical 6-10: no new target model, Grupo Vale's own is the target.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: First-company process area cut over to Grupo Vale's processes and systems
First-company stabilization after cutover, with open issues closed

phases.why: Archetype has no Implementation phase. Process areas cut over two at a time at the first company only, then a stabilization period.

sizing.levers: Moving the first-company cutover after the board meeting saves 8-11 weeks; running all three process areas at once or diagnosing two companies saves less.
